scenario: I live in NYC and have been wanting to go out for hikes with my dog, who suffers a lot from being cooped up. The problem is I have no car, and there is nowhere to hike nearby. The trains that run from the city to places upstate, where I can hike, have no-dog policies or significantly restrict the size of the dog. My dog is an eighty-pound golden retriever mutt, so he is too big for the train's size policy. The thought occurred to me to put a service dog vest on my non-service dog to pretend that he is one. And if anyone asks, I can say he is a seizure-response dog. That way, I can get on the train with him and have a reason for why he’s with me. My dog is well-behaved and has the look of a service dog, so I think I can get away with it. If I put a service dog vest on my non-service dog to pretend that he is one, then my dog can get time outdoors. If I do not do this, there won’t be any other way for me to take him hiking.
choice: I decide to put a service dog vest on my non-service dog to pretend that he is one
